references.text: Jesus went again to the place on the other side of the Jordan, where John had first baptized, and stayed there. [ref:Joh 10:40|John 10:40] confirms that Bethany beyond the Jordan was the place where John baptized, the same place mentioned in 1:28.
In [ref:Joh 3:26|John 3:26], John's disciples refer to the one who was with him "on the other side of the Jordan," a clear reference to the place mentioned in 1:28 where John testified about Jesus.
[ref:Joh 3:23|John 3:23] mentions that John also baptized in Aenon, near Salim, showing that John had several baptismal sites, contrasting with Bethany by the Jordan mentioned in 1:28.

[ref:Joh 1:19|John 1:19] introduces the testimony given by John the Baptist to the priests and Levites sent from Jerusalem – that testimony which took place in Bethany by the Jordan according to verse 28.

[ref:Luk 3:3|Luke 3:3] tells us that John came into all the country around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins, confirming the geographical location of his ministry along the Jordan River, also mentioned in John 1:28.

[ref:Matt 3:5-6|Matthew 3:5-6] describes how people from Jerusalem, all Judea, and all the region around the Jordan came out to John and were baptized by him in the Jordan River, a parallel to his baptismal ministry at Bethany by the Jordan.

[ref:Mark 1:4-5|Mark 1:4-5] tells of John appearing in the wilderness and baptizing in the Jordan River. This is a synoptic parallel to John's baptismal activity geographically located in Bethany by the Jordan in John 1:28.
[ref:Joh 11:1|John 11:1] mentions another Bethany, the village of Mary and Martha, near Jerusalem. This is distinct from Bethany by the Jordan in 1:28, and the two places should not be confused.
